newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: SGBT raises SAirGroup 1996 loss estimate.
newsitem.headline: SGBT raises SAirGroup 1996 loss estimate.

text.p: Societe Generale Bank & Trust (SGBT) said it had raised its estimate for the 1996 loss of SAirGroup following the unexpectedly high loss at Sabena, 49.5 percent owned by the Swiss airline group.

SGBT analyst Dieter Winet wrote in a research note that he had raised his estimated 1996 loss to 70 Swiss francs per share from a previous estimate of 34.0 francs. In 1995 SAirGroup, the parent of the Swissair airline, lost 64 francs per share.
The results from Sabena "come as a sobering reminder of the critical situation facing the SAirGroup subsidiary," Winet said.
Sabena reported a 1996 loss of 8.9 billion Belgian francs, or around 370 million Swiss francs, including 4.1 billion in exceptional charges.
Winet expects Sabena's loss to negatively impact SAirGroup's 1996 result with around 100 million francs after tax, up from a previous estimate of a negative impact of 50 million.
"We expect SAirGroup to write down its holding in Sabena to zero in its balance sheet in order to regain its freedom to manoeuvre," Winet said.
He said this would put the company in position to concentrate on restoring its airline business to operating profit during 1997 without distractions or financial risk.
